newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Liton mulls buying General Instrument.
newsitem.headline: Liton mulls buying General Instrument.

text.p: Taiwan's Liton Electronic group said on Thursday it was considering buying the semiconductor department of General Instrument 's Taiwan unit.
"We are evaluating whether to make the deal, but we have yet to make a final decision," Stephen King, a spokesman for Liton group, told Reuters by telephone.
The local Economic Daily News said on Thursday the deal would cost the Liton group some US$250 million.
King said the report was speculation by the newspaper. He declined to confirm or deny it.
"Both sides have signed a non-disclosure agreement, so we cannot announce details unless we finalise the deal," he said.
The semiconductor department of General Instrument Taiwan Ltd produces diode rectifiers, a key component for making power supplies and other electronic products.
The Liton group includes three key members: opto-electronics and power supply maker Liton, monitor maker Lite-On Technology Corp, and keyboard and scanner maker Silitek Corp.
The group's combined sales reached around T$45 billion in 1996, King said. "We hope for a more than 30-percent sales growth in 1997," he said.
